# Summary of the Scottish National Party (SNP) Manifesto 2015

The 2015 SNP manifesto, titled "Stronger for Scotland," presented the party's vision for increased Scottish representation and influence at Westminster, led by Nicola Sturgeon's pledge to make Scotland's voice heard more loudly than ever before.

## Core Economic Position

The SNP firmly rejected austerity, proposing instead modest public spending increases while still reducing the deficit as a percentage of national income. Their approach would make £140 billion more available compared to Conservative plans over the parliament. They advocated for progressive taxation including restoring the 50p top tax rate, a mansion tax, bank levy, and crackdowns on tax avoidance. The party committed to never putting the Conservatives in power and would work with other parties to form an anti-Tory majority.

## Key Policy Priorities

**Fair Pay and Jobs**: The manifesto proposed increasing the minimum wage to £8.70 by 2020 and expanding living wage adoption. They sought seed funding for a Scottish Business Development Bank, reduced Air Passenger Duty, and stronger infrastructure investment including high-speed rail connecting Scotland to England.

**Public Services**: The SNP pledged £2 billion additional NHS funding by 2020-21 and protection from privatisation. They supported expanding free childcare to 30 hours weekly, maintaining free university tuition, and delivering 30,000 Modern Apprenticeships annually.

**Welfare Reform**: Central to their agenda was abolishing the Bedroom Tax, halting Universal Credit rollout, reversing disability benefit cuts, increasing Carer's Allowance, and reforming the harsh sanctions regime.

**Housing**: They backed building 100,000 affordable homes annually across the UK.

## Opposition to Trident

The SNP strongly opposed renewing Trident nuclear weapons, arguing the £100 billion cost should instead fund public services.

## Further Devolution

While restating their belief in independence, the manifesto focused on securing the promises made during the 2014 referendum campaign, pushing for full fiscal responsibility and powers over employment, welfare, taxation and the economy beyond the Smith Commission recommendations.

## Protecting Scottish Interests

SNP MPs would vote against any Westminster measure reducing Scotland's funding and oppose EU withdrawal without majority consent from all four UK nations.
